title: Natural comparison between the explicit principal Cech bicomplex total and the existing total functor
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}r\to A$. Define $B(F)$ to be the integer-indexed bicomplex with columns $C_p(F)$ and horizontal maps $h_p(F)$ from [def-sc-principal-cech-columns], using their square-zero property [lem-sc-principal-cech-horizontal-square]. Define $B(i)$ by the product of the section maps in each column. Then there is a natural isomorphism of functors from integer-indexed complexes of module sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ to integer-indexed $A$-module complexes, $\operatorname{principalCechFunctor}(r,f)\cong B\,;\,\operatorname{Tot}$, where the left functor is [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total] and $\operatorname{Tot}$ is Mathlib's diagonal-coproduct total with differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$. No boundedness assumption is made.

proof.text: Construct B(F) by CochainComplex.of with product column objects C_p(F), horizontal differential h_p(F), and the square-zero theorem. The vertical chain-map compatibility and naturality were proved in the explicit column construction. Define B(i) columnwise; naturality of h verifies its chain-map equation.

In total degree n regroup the subset coordinates by p=card(S)-1 and q=n-p. The row index is empty outside 0,...,r-1, by nonempty cardinality and card(S)≤r. The diagonal coproduct is therefore a finite product of the degreewise section coordinates. Its degreewise inverse sends each coordinate to its unique column summand.

Check the differentials on the degreewise coordinates. Mathlib totalization has horizontal sign 1 and vertical sign (-1)^p, giving the same alternating restrictions and vertical differential as principalCechDifferentialValue. The specification of principalCechDifferential_exists identifies the chosen differential with this formula.

Compose with principalCechObjIso. The coefficient map specification in principalCechFunctor_exists and the product-map formula show that the degreewise comparison commutes with all coefficient chain maps. Thus the chain isomorphisms form a natural isomorphism. For the empty cover both sides are zero.
